concept.name: Rolling minimum
concept.definition: The rolling minimum is the lowest value of a series within a trailing window of fixed length that slides forward one observation at a time. Together with the rolling maximum it defines the lower boundary of channel indicators such as Donchian channels.
concept.intuition: At each point, look back over the last N bars and ask: what was the lowest price seen? The level ratchets as time passes and old lows expire from the window.
concept.mechanics: For window length w, compute min over observations x_{t−w+1}…x_t at each t; implementations such as pandas rolling().min() label at the window's right edge and produce NaN until the window fills unless min_periods is set.
concept.formula: RMin_t = min(x_{t−w+1}, …, x_t), where w is the window length.
concept.failure_modes: Like the rolling maximum, it jumps discontinuously when an extreme exits the window and is entirely defined by the chosen window length; centered windows leak future data into the past.
concept.misconceptions: The rolling minimum is not a support level in any market-microstructure sense — it is purely the trailing extreme over an arbitrary lookback.
concept.example: With a 20-day rolling minimum on daily lows, if the lowest low of the last 20 days is 96.10, the lower Donchian line sits at 96.10 today.
